Gardening in temperate climates

Starting a vegetable garden in spring requires planning for frost dates, soil preparation, and choosing varieties suited to your hardiness zone. Raised beds improve drainage for heavy clay.

Companion planting reduces pest pressure without chemicals. Basil near tomatoes and marigolds along bed borders are reliable combinations many growers use every season.

Water deeply but less often to encourage root growth. Morning irrigation reduces evaporation and helps foliage dry before evening, which limits fungal issues on leaves.
